mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 620d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 6 Series 620d engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£2,800 for a used B47D20 unit, £2,800-£4,500 for a reconditioned engine, and £3,800-£5,800 for a fully rebuilt engine with warranty. Supply & fit adds £520-£780 in specialist labour (8-12 hours). Used engines offer the lowest upfront cost with limited warranty; reconditioned engines sit in the mid-range with some new parts fitted; rebuilt engines are the most expensive but fully restored to factory spec with a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR cooler failure in a BMW 6 Series 620d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include coolant loss without visible external leaks, increased exhaust smoke, decreased fuel efficiency, and EGR-related fault codes. In advanced cases, the engine may overheat or show a coolant warning light. If you suspect EGR cooler failure, have it inspected immediately - internal coolant leaks can cause serious engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 620d?

acceptedAnswer.text: With average values of £16,000-£20,000, a full rebuilt engine at £3,800-£5,800 represents 20-35% of the vehicle's value - making replacement financially viable for most examples. If your 620d is in good condition with reasonable mileage, a rebuilt engine can extend its life by 150,000+ miles. For sub-£15,000 cars, consider a used engine or targeted repair; for £15,000-£20,000 cars, a reconditioned engine is viable; for £20,000+ cars, a rebuilt engine with warranty makes strong financial sense.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 620d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 6 Series 620d engine replacement takes 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The B47D20 is a four-cylinder unit with reasonable engine bay access, but the G32's complex electronics and xDrive variants add labour time. Most specialists offer collection/delivery options nationwide with same-day dispatch available for in-stock engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 620d and 630d engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 620d uses the 2.0L B47D20 four-cylinder diesel (190hp, 400Nm), while the 630d uses the 3.0L B57D30 six-cylinder diesel (261hp, 620Nm). The 620d offers better fuel economy (up to 58.9mpg) and lower running costs, but the 630d delivers significantly more torque and a smoother, more refined driving experience.

The B47D20 is considered significantly more reliable than the older N47 diesel. BMW relocated the timing chain to the front of the engine, addressing the N47's notorious chain failure issue. However, EGR cooler failure and DPF clogging remain common concerns, particularly on vehicles used mainly for short urban journeys.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 620d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 620d Gran Turismo joined the G32 6 Series range in July 2018 as the entry-level diesel variant. Slotting in below the six-cylinder 630d, the 620d brought BMW's latest B47 four-cylinder diesel to the large executive liftback, offering a compelling blend of efficiency and refinement. The 620d remained in production through the G32's lifecycle until 2023.

milestones.description: July 2018 - B47D20, 2.0L four-cylinder turbo-diesel, 190hp, introduced as the entry-level 620d Gran Turismo
2020 - B47D20 (140kW / 190hp) fitted to 620d and 620d xDrive variants
July 2020 - B47D20B with mild-hybrid technology introduced, 163hp or 190hp variants available
G32 6 Series Gran Turismo production ends

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 620d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 6 Series 620d is powered by the B47D20 family of 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo-diesel engines - BMW's modern replacement for the earlier N47. While significantly more reliable than its predecessor, the B47 is not without its weaknesses. Rebuilt B47D20 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded EGR and cooling system components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 620d B47D20 Suffers Coolant Leaks
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can fail internally, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust stream. This mixture of coolant, hot exhaust gases, and soot leads to excessive carbon buildup and, in severe cases, can pose a fire risk. BMW issued technical campaigns addressing this issue across the B47, N47 and N57 engine families.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before secondary damage

With average values around £16,000-£20,000, a full rebuilt engine at £3,800-£5,800 represents 20-35% of the vehicle's value - comfortably within the "safe" threshold. For higher-mileage examples approaching £15,000, a reconditioned engine or targeted EGR repair may offer better value.
problems.recommendation: If your 620d is showing EGR-related warning lights or coolant loss without visible external leaks, have the EGR cooler inspected immediately. A specialist EGR cooler replacement at £500-£900 is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement and addresses the root cause. Only consider a full rebuilt engine if the EGR failure has caused secondary damage to the DPF, turbo, or injectors.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging - Urban Driving Shortens B47D20 Life
problems.rootCause: Like all modern diesel engines, the B47D20's DPF requires regular motorway driving to initiate passive regeneration. Short journeys and stop-start driving prevent the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, leading to soot buildup, warning lights, and reduced performance.

problems.recommendation: If your 620d is used mainly around town, book a forced DPF regeneration every 12-18 months as preventative maintenance. If the DPF warning light is already on, address it immediately - ignoring a clogged DPF will lead to much more expensive turbo and engine repairs.
